DECK: Discipleship Experience (Section 7) Bible Experience I

Q1. According to Biblical Interpretation, the defining quality God prioritizes in those entrusted to pass on doctrine is:
A. Charisma
B. Anointing
C. Faithfulness
D. Eloquence
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson prioritizes faithfulness in preserving doctrine and handing it on.
REF: INTRODUCTION TO BIBLICAL INTERPRETATION III — [11:56]–[14:32] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: 2 Timothy 2:2–3; Deuteronomy 4; Galatians 1:8

Q2. Final authority of Scripture means that the Word of God has:
A. The last word on all matters of faith, doctrine and practice
B. The final word wherever questions of right and wrong arise
C. Supreme authority over doctrine and the believer's spiritual life
D. Ultimate authority whenever human reasoning reaches its limits
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson says Scripture is the ultimate authority in matters of faith, doctrine, and practice.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW I — [00:16]–[01:26] (approximate range)

Q3. According to the lesson on hermeneutics, the apostles and prophets were given the responsibility of:
A. Creating new doctrine based on their personal encounters with God
B. Translating Old Testament prophecy into culturally relevant Christian teaching
C. Establishing which Old Testament passages should remain authoritative
D. Receiving revelation and laying the foundation of doctrine
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The lesson assigns the apostles and prophets the role of receiving revealed truth and laying doctrine’s foundation.
REF: HERMENEUTICS (PART 1) I — [17:59]–[18:51] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Ephesians 3

Q4. The statement "Doctrine is not your invention" primarily means that doctrine:
A. Is established independently of the individual who encounters it.
B. Is inherited from the church and therefore should not be questioned.
C. Is determined by the interpretation of Scripture already accepted by believers.
D. Is established before an individual studies Scripture and therefore requires no interpretation.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson presents doctrine as established independently of an individual’s personal interpretation.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW II — [00:57]–[02:04] (approximate range)

Q5. A believer who has become established in fundamental doctrine reaches a stage where Bible study should increasingly help them:
A. Discover increasingly radical interpretations of familiar passages
B. Move from personal study into teaching ministry
C. Replace foundational teaching with deeper and more advanced revelations
D. Appreciate what they have always known rather than constantly searching for what is new
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: Bible study can deepen appreciation of established truth rather than focus on finding something new.
REF: INTRODUCTION TO BIBLICAL INTERPRETATION I — [01:12]–[02:59] (approximate range)

Q6. Which of the following is the Greek word for revelation?
A. Rhema
B. Logos
C. Gnosis
D. Apocalypsis
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The lesson identifies apocalypsis as the Greek word for revelation.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW II — [04:41]

Q7. In Having a Biblical Worldview, "All Scripture is given by inspiration of God" establishes primarily that:
A. The human writers were moved by God in the process of writing Scripture.
B. Scripture communicates God's will through the experiences of its writers.
C. God is the source of all Scripture.
D. The content of Scripture ultimately reflects God's intention through human authorship.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson explicitly says inspiration establishes God as the source of Scripture.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW I — [09:00]–[10:11] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: 2 Timothy 3:16–17

Q8. According to the lesson on Having a Biblical Worldview, what should happen when a believer discovers that an ideology they hold is wrong?
A. The Word should straighten the ideology rather than the believer searching for a church that reinforces it.
B. The believer should retain the conviction until they receive a clearer personal revelation.
C. The believer should consider whether the ideology is culturally acceptable before changing it.
D. The believer should compare the ideology with the prevailing interpretation within their church.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson says the Word should correct a believer’s ideology, not merely confirm it.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW II — [08:44]–[09:26] (approximate range)

Q9. The Greek word musterion in Ephesians 3, is explained in the lesson as referring to:
A. A truth that can only be understood by spiritually mature believers
B. A truth deliberately withheld because God had not yet decided to reveal it
C. A supernatural truth that remains inaccessible through ordinary reading
D. Something concealed that is now revealed
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The lesson defines musterion as something concealed that is now revealed.
REF: HERMENEUTICS (PART 1) I — [01:06]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Ephesians 3:1

Q10. The Latin expression for faith alone is:
A. Sola Scriptura
B. Sola Gratia
C. Soli Deo Gloria
D. Sola Fide
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The lesson gives sola fide as the Latin expression for faith alone.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW I — [03:38]

Q11. The phrase "retain it in its originality and hand it over to people who will hand it over to others" is presented as the practical evidence of:
A. Faithfulness to an orthodox faith that is not subject to personal invention
B. Spiritual maturity demonstrated through the ability to reproduce one's interpretation
C. Apostolic authority demonstrated through successive generations of teachers
D. Accurate Bible study demonstrated through the ability to explain Scripture creatively
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson identifies preserving and passing on doctrine without inventing new interpretations as evidence of faithfulness.
REF: INTRODUCTION TO BIBLICAL INTERPRETATION III — [11:56]–[14:32] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: 2 Timothy 2; Deuteronomy 4; Galatians 1

Q12. The lesson on hermeneutics describes Christ as "the most important piece in Bible interpretation." What does this mean within the specific argument being made?
A. Every biblical passage must contain the literal name "Jesus" before it can be interpreted
B. Christ provides the interpretive key for understanding the Old Testament's types, shadows and symbols
C. The New Testament should be studied independently of the Old Testament because Christ replaced its message
D. Every Old Testament passage should be interpreted exclusively as a direct prediction of Jesus' earthly ministry
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson presents Christ as the key to understanding the Old Testament’s symbols and types.
REF: HERMENEUTICS (PART 2) I — [13:48]–[16:49] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: 2 Corinthians 4

Q13. In Having a Biblical Worldview, the word "so" in John 3:16 is explained as primarily communicating:
A. The intensity with which God loved the world
B. The magnitude of God's love for humanity
C. The depth of God's emotional affection toward the world
D. The manner in which God demonstrated His love
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The lesson explains “so” as describing how God showed His love, rather than its intensity.
REF: INTRODUCTION TO BIBLICAL INTERPRETATION II — [09:24]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: John 3:16

Q14. God's plan for the church, as presented in the lesson on Bible Interpretation, is that believers:
A. Become sufficiently grounded to recognize sound teaching when they hear it
B. Come into the unanimity of the faith with accuracy and clarity
C. Become increasingly dependent on the teaching ministry of their pastor
D. Develop enough personal revelation to contribute meaningfully when they gather
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson describes the church’s goal as believers sharing the faith with accuracy and clarity.
REF: INTRODUCTION TO BIBLICAL INTERPRETATION I — [00:16]–[01:12] (approximate range)

Q15. Why does the lesson on Having a Biblical Worldview connect Paul's statement about failing to provide for one's relatives with denying the faith?
A. Because Christian families have a specific obligation to financially support one another
B. Because practical care is one of the strongest ways believers demonstrate their righteousness.
C. Because certain conduct is so inconsistent with professed faith that its absence can contradict the profession itself.
D. Because failure to care for relatives demonstrates that the believer has misunderstood the doctrine of grace.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson treats the absence of practical care in this example as inconsistent with a profession of Christian faith.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW II — [14:41]–[15:58] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Added from online research: 1 Timothy 5:8 (https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%205:8&version=ESV)

Q16. What is the strongest indication that biblical interpretation is being done correctly?
A. The believer becomes more confident when defending doctrine
B. The believer develops greater knowledge of historical and theological details
C. The believer becomes increasingly skilled at identifying erroneous interpretations
D. The knowledge drives the believer toward worship and greater response to God
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The lesson says correctly interpreted knowledge should lead to worship and a greater response to God.
REF: INTRODUCTION TO BIBLICAL INTERPRETATION III — [16:44]–[20:09] (approximate range)

Q17. What does "where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty" mean in its immediate interpretive context?
A. Freedom to express oneself physically during church services
B. Freedom from the veil so that believers can behold the glory and intent of God's writings
C. Freedom from the need to interpret Scripture according to its original context
D. Freedom from the authority of the Old Testament because the Spirit has replaced Scripture
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: In context, liberty means the veil is removed so the writings’ meaning and God’s glory can be seen.
REF: HERMENEUTICS (PART 2) I — [17:45]–[18:32] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: 2 Corinthians 3:14–18

Q18. The lesson on hermeneutics uses the description of Christ as "the express image of his person" to emphasize that:
A. Christ's teachings are more practical than those of the prophets
B. Christ represents the cultural fulfillment of Old Testament prophecy
C. Christ is the final prophet through whom the Old Testament can be interpreted
D. In Christ, we understand exactly who God is
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The lesson says Christ reveals exactly who God is.
REF: HERMENEUTICS (PART 1) II — [01:13]–[02:57] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Hebrews 1:3

Q19. Which pair correctly matches the biblical statement with the figure of speech identified in the hermeneutics lesson?
A. "I am the door" - simile
B. "Behold, I send you forth as sheep" - metaphor
C. "I am the vine" - hyperbole
D. "I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves" - simile
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The lesson identifies the comparison using “as” as a simile.
REF: HERMENEUTICS (PART 1) I — [09:27]–[10:36] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: 2 Corinthians 11:16; Matthew 10:16; John 10:9

Q20. Which combination accurately reflects the languages identified in the lesson?
A. Old Testament - Hebrew and Aramaic; New Testament - Koine Greek
B. Old Testament - Hebrew and Greek; New Testament - Aramaic and Greek
C. Old Testament - Hebrew only; New Testament - Koine Greek and Latin
D. Old Testament - Aramaic and Latin; New Testament - Hebrew and Koine Greek
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson identifies Hebrew and Aramaic for the Old Testament and Koine Greek for the New Testament.
REF: HERMENEUTICS (PART 1) I — [05:26]–[06:27] (approximate range)

Q21. Stephen's description of his Jewish audience as "uncircumcised in the heart" is used in the lesson on hermeneutics to establish what distinction?
A. Physical circumcision could exist without the spiritual reality it was intended to signify
B. Physical circumcision was never actually commanded by God
C. The Jews had abandoned the practice of circumcision before Stephen addressed them
D. Circumcision of the heart was exclusively a New Testament doctrine with no Old Testament precedent
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson distinguishes physical circumcision from the spiritual reality of circumcision of the heart.
REF: HERMENEUTICS (PART 2) II — [14:44]–[16:44] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Acts 7:51; Ephesians 2:11; Philippians 3:2

Q22. Which interpretation does the lesson on Hermeneutics explicitly reject concerning the statement "the letter kills"?
A. That "the letter" specifically refers to the law written on stones
B. That the statement refers to the law in contrast with the ministry of the Spirit
C. That "the letter" means the entire Bible is incapable of giving life without a personal rhema
D. That Paul was contrasting the ministry associated with the law with the ministry of the New Testament
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson rejects applying “the letter kills” to the entire Bible or claiming Scripture needs a personal rhema to give life.
REF: HERMENEUTICS (PART 2) I — [06:32]–[07:19] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: John 3; 2 Corinthians 3; John 6

Q23. Which statement most accurately distinguishes "sundry times" from "diverse manners" according to the lesson?
A. Sundry times concerns different prophets, while diverse manners concerns different generations
B. Sundry times concerns prophecy, while diverse manners concerns Scripture
C. Sundry times refers to communication in many different parts, while diverse manners refers to different modes of communication
D. Sundry times refers to Old Testament communication, while diverse manners refers exclusively to New Testament communication
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson distinguishes communication given in many parts from communication delivered through different modes.
REF: HERMENEUTICS (PART 1) II — [02:57]–[03:55]; HERMENEUTICS (PART 2) I — [01:46]–[02:44] (approximate ranges)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Hebrews 1:1

Q24. The instruction to read "per book, per chapter" is specifically intended to prevent the interpreter from:
A. Relying on individual verses instead of the full counsel of Scripture
B. Removing a text from its context and assigning meaning based on the words alone
C. Reading Scripture according to personal experiences and previously held convictions
D. Reading Scripture according to personal experiences and previously held convictions
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: Reading by book and chapter helps prevent taking a text out of its context.
REF: INTRODUCTION TO BIBLICAL INTERPRETATION II — [03:33]–[04:26] (approximate range)

Q25. Romans 16:16 is primarily an example of which interpretation barrier according to the lesson on Biblical Interpretation?
A. Translation
B. Language
C. Culture
D. Doctrine
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson uses Romans 16:16 to show how culture affects interpretation of a biblical instruction.
REF: HERMENEUTICS (PART 1) I — [12:45]–[15:57] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Romans 16:16 | Also cited in lesson segment: John 15:5; John 12; John 21:25; 1 Corinthians 16:21; 1 Corinthians 2

Q26. According to the hermeneutics lesson, why can an honest and careful translation still make Bible interpretation difficult?
A. Translators inevitably change the doctrines of the original writers
B. Biblical languages cannot adequately express spiritual realities in English
C. English translations necessarily remove figures of speech from the text
D. Some meaning and nuance can become less immediately clear through translation
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: A faithful translation can still make the intended meaning difficult to understand, so interpretation may be needed.
REF: HERMENEUTICS (PART 1) I — [05:26]–[06:27]; INTRODUCTION TO BIBLICAL INTERPRETATION II — [05:56]–[08:17] (approximate ranges)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: 2 Corinthians 1:13

Q27. Which text does the lesson on Bible Interpretation identify as having had an exceptionally significant impact on world history?
A. John 3:16
B. John 1:1
C. 2 Corinthians 2:11
D. Galatians 3:11
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The lesson identifies Galatians 3:11 as having had exceptional historical impact.
REF: INTRODUCTION TO BIBLICAL INTERPRETATION I — [07:05]–[09:26] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Galatians 3:11 | Also cited in lesson segment: John 3:16

Q28. In Having a Biblical Worldview, "Your word is a lamp unto my feet and a light unto my path" was used to mean:
A. Scripture gives believers insight into God's specific plan for their future.
B. Scripture orders the believer's steps and determines how they navigate life.
C. Scripture provides principles by which believers can evaluate their circumstances.
D. Scripture gives believers sufficient wisdom to make decisions without external counsel.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson uses the verse to describe Scripture as a guide for navigating life and ordering one’s steps.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW I — [06:51]–[07:50] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Added from online research: Psalm 119:105 (https://www.esv.org/verses/Psalm%2B119%3A105/)

Q29. Which combination best reflects the progression identified in Isaiah 53 within the lesson on hermeneutics?
A. Christ's incarnation -> earthly ministry -> ascension -> enthronement
B. Christ's rejection and suffering -> bearing of sin -> death -> resurrection implied
C. Israel's rejection -> restoration -> establishment of the church -> final judgment
D. The law -> the prophets -> the gospel -> justification by works
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson traces Christ’s rejection and suffering, sin-bearing, death, and implied resurrection through Isaiah 53.
REF: HERMENEUTICS (PART 2) II — [03:05]–[07:13] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Isaiah 53 | Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 10; Acts 8

Q30. The biblical worldview becomes evident when the Word of God becomes the believer's:
A. Standard for evaluating spiritual experiences
B. Foundation for establishing doctrinal convictions
C. Guide for making decisions concerning Christian practice
D. Lens through which they see the world
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The lesson describes a biblical worldview as seeing the world through the lens of God’s Word.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW I — [06:51]–[07:50] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: 2 Timothy 3:16, 17

Q31. The speaker says that, in Protestant circles, the Latin expression sola scriptura means:
A. Faith alone
B. Grace alone
C. Scripture alone
D. To the glory of God alone
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker identifies sola scriptura as the Latin expression for Scripture alone, distinct from the faith, grace and glory-of-God expressions.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW I — [02:38]

Q32. According to the speaker, what happened when only a few people had access to the Scriptures?
A. Church practice stayed more carefully tied to what Scripture taught
B. Church leaders became more cautious about adding new practices to worship
C. Guardrails were easily removed and extremes were entertained in the church
D. Believers became more devoted to studying the Latin text of the Bible
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker says limited access made it easy for guardrails to be taken out of the way and for extremes to be entertained, which the Reformers opposed.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW I — [02:38]

Q33. Which set of expressions does the speaker list as the Reformers' Latin 'alone' statements?
A. Faith alone, grace alone, to the glory of Christ alone, and the church alone
B. Faith alone, works alone, to the glory of God alone, and Scripture alone
C. Faith alone, grace alone, the priesthood alone, and Scripture alone
D. Faith alone, grace alone, to the glory of God alone, and Scripture alone
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: Describing the Reformers' conviction, the speaker lists sola fide (faith alone), grace alone, to the glory of God alone, and Scripture alone.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW I — [03:38]

Q34. Which practice does the speaker give as an example of the church doing things that, in the Reformers' view, were not biblical?
A. Allowing ordinary believers to read the Bible in their own language
B. Charging payments for sin at different prices to lift a person's sins
C. Refusing to recant when pressured by religious authorities
D. Teaching that the just shall live by faith and by grace alone
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker's example is the payments made for sin, with different prices for different sins, after which the sins would supposedly be lifted.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW I — [02:38; 03:38]

Q35. Why does the speaker say believers should understand how far church history has come?
A. So they will not undo progress won by people who died for believers' liberty
B. So they can trace which denominations keep the oldest church practices
C. So they can finish correcting the errors the Reformers left unaddressed
D. So they can decide which church traditions deserve equal weight with Scripture
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker says to understand church history so that we will not set back the progress people made, since they died for the liberty believers have in Christ.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW I — [03:38; 04:35]

Q36. According to the lesson on the final authority of Scripture, what must be judged by the authority of the Scriptures?
A. Only church traditions, since experiences are guided by the Holy Spirit
B. Every experience and every church tradition, however long it has been practiced
C. Only personal experiences, since church traditions are protected by their age
D. Doctrine and practice, but not claims of dreams and visions
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker states that every experience must be judged by the authority of Scripture, and that church traditions must be judged by it no matter how long they have been practiced.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW I — [04:35]

Q37. What point does the speaker make with the Samaritan woman's words, 'Our fathers worshipped on this mountain'?
A. Jesus approved worship that had been handed down over centuries
B. Long-standing devotional practice gives a tradition its authority
C. The Samaritans' descent from Abraham made their worship acceptable
D. A practice can continue for centuries and still be wrong
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker says she referred to centuries of devotional practice, yet Jesus told her she did not know what she worshipped, showing that something can be done for centuries and be wrong.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW I — [05:49]
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: John 4

Q38. How does the speaker respond to believers who say 'put scripture aside' when explaining what they want to do?
A. Scripture may yield to personal conviction on matters the Bible does not mention
B. Scripture may be set aside once a believer has prayed about the decision
C. Scripture should be set aside only when a church tradition disagrees with it
D. Scripture is never put aside; the Word of God must influence how a believer reasons
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker says the Word of God must influence how you reason and that you never put scripture aside again.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW I — [07:50]
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: 2 Timothy 3:16, 17

Q39. How does the speaker answer the objection that the Bible cannot be God's word because it was written by men?
A. Only the portions written by prophets count as God's word, while the rest is human
B. It can be both, because God is sovereign and can work through the freedom of men
C. God dictated the text word for word, so the writers' lives played no part in it
D. The writers' own views are mixed into the text, so readers must separate them out
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker answers that it can be both, because God is sovereign and can walk with the freedom of men, arranging the writers' experiences so that what they wrote was His will.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW I — [11:02; 11:54]

Q40. What does the speaker use the story of Joseph to illustrate about God's leading?
A. A dream from God must be explained from Scripture before anyone can act on it
B. God's purposes depend on people making the right political choices at key moments
C. People can act in ways they think are free while their actions advance God's purpose
D. God always gives explicit step-by-step directions before a person acts on a dream
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker says God did not have to tell Joseph to go to Egypt; everyone acted in a manner they thought free, yet contributed to the prophetic story and its intended end.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW I — [10:11; 11:02]
BIBLE: Added from online research: Genesis 50:20 (https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis%2050:20&version=ESV)

Q41. According to the speaker, how did God change Peter's belief that salvation was for the Jews alone?
A. By a trance of animals, then men from Cornelius's house arriving
B. By explaining from the Scriptures that salvation is for all men
C. By a letter from church leaders in Jerusalem urging him to go
D. By Cornelius's household arguing the point from the Old Testament
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker says God did not explain from Scripture but showed Peter a trance of animals, and the people from Cornelius's house were already at his door when he woke.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW I — [12:46]
BIBLE: Added from online research: Acts 10 (https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2010&version=ESV)

Q42. Once you have established what the Word of God says, the speaker says that is:
A. The end of all arguments
B. A starting point to be weighed against tradition
C. The start of a deeper debate
D. The point at which personal experience should be consulted
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker says that the moment you establish what the Word of God says, that is the end of all arguments.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW I — [01:26]

Q43. What does the speaker say 'profitable for doctrine' means for someone reading the Bible?
A. The believer is given freedom to choose between competing teachings
B. Each reader receives a personal meaning suited to their circumstances
C. Reading the Bible, the believer arrives at a doctrinal position
D. The believer is prepared to defend any church's position
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker explains that 'profitable for doctrine' means that when I read the Bible, I arrive at a doctrinal position.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW II — [00:17]
BIBLE: Added from online research: 2 Timothy 3:16 (https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Timothy%203:16&version=ESV)

Q44. What contrast does the speaker draw between Catholics, Reformed, Lutherans and Methodists on one hand and Pentecostals on the other?
A. The first groups disagree among themselves, while Pentecostals agree on every point
B. The first groups hold uniform beliefs, while Pentecostals have no written beliefs
C. The first groups rely on tradition, while Pentecostals rely on Scripture alone
D. The others know what they believe, but for Pentecostals it depends on the church
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker says Catholics, Reformed, Lutherans and Methodists know what they believe, but among Pentecostals it depends on the church you attend.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW II — [00:50; 00:57]

Q45. When reading the Bible, what does the speaker say he wants to understand about Paul?
A. How Paul's teaching has been applied within each denomination
B. What Paul actually believed, since some preach things Paul never said
C. What Paul would say about the questions raised by modern culture
D. Which of Paul's letters carry the most authority for the church today
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker says he wants to see and understand what Paul believed, noting that some people have accused Paul of saying things he never said.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW II — [04:16]

Q46. What does the speaker say about the Spirit of God in relation to the written Word?
A. The Spirit of God will never contradict the written Word
B. The Spirit guides each believer's doctrine apart from the written Word
C. The Spirit may extend the written Word with teachings it does not contain
D. The Spirit may correct the written Word where it is unclear
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker insists doctrine is established, not 'as the Spirit leads', and that the Spirit of God will never contradict the written word.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW II — [01:39; 01:55]

Q47. How does the speaker define doctrine?
A. A teaching adopted whenever it feels spiritually fresh
B. A set of opinions agreed upon by a local congregation
C. A personal conviction formed through private revelation
D. A long-established, inherited way of thinking or acting
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker states that doctrine is a long established, inherited way of thinking or acting.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW II — [04:06]

Q48. What criticism does the speaker make about the term 'rhema'?
A. The term describes the way Paul's letters were first received
B. The term wrongly replaces the Greek word for the written Scriptures
C. Such phrases have been coined to excuse exegetical understanding of the Bible
D. The term is a legitimate name for the Spirit's present-day guidance
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker says we have coined phrases like rhema to excuse exegetical understanding of the Bible, and that people who don't know Greek have confused us.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW II — [04:41]

Q49. What does the speaker say the Greek word translated 'reproof' in 2 Timothy 3:16 actually means?
A. Instruction, in the sense of teaching righteousness
B. Conviction, so that it could be translated 'proof'
C. Correction, as most readers assume it means
D. Rebuke, in the sense of a sharp spoken warning
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: Using the lexicon, the speaker says people assume reproof means correction, but the Greek word actually means conviction and should be translated proof.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW II — [05:30; 06:02]

Q50. When explaining God to atheists, which does the speaker call the ultimate evidence?
A. The Bible
B. Nature
C. Personal experiences
D. Good arguments
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker thanks God for experiences and good arguments and says nature can be used, but the Bible is the ultimate evidence and the reason he believes.
REF: HAVING A BIBLICAL WORLDVIEW II — [06:17; 07:16]

A. Think of a treasury, something by which wealth is kept
B. Think of a dispenser, something by which something is released
C. Think of a covenant, something by which a promise is sealed
D. Think of a steward, something by which a house is managed
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker explains dispensation by saying to think of a dispenser, something by which something is released, so the grace of God is communicated through Paul.
REF: HERMENEUTICS (PART 1) I — [01:06]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Ephesians 3:2 | Also cited in lesson segment: Ephesians 3:1

Q102. What picture does the speaker use for the Old Testament's communication of God's mystery?
A. A man who writes a letter and seals it
B. A man who speaks from behind a closed door
C. A man who says something with his mouth covered
D. A man who whispers a message to a friend
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker says the Old Testament is akin to a man who says something but with his mouth covered, which is why some readers do not understand it.
REF: HERMENEUTICS (PART 1) I — [01:56]

Q103. Why does the speaker say the New Testament seems clearer than the Old Testament?
A. God changed His character between the Old and New Testaments
B. The Old Testament was written for a much smaller audience of readers
C. God did not change; He stopped speaking in mysteries and spoke plainly
D. The New Testament writers used a simpler and more modern vocabulary
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker says it's not as if God changed; now God no longer spoke with mysteries and just spoke in plain language.
REF: HERMENEUTICS (PART 1) I — [02:51]

Q104. What does the speaker conclude from 2 Corinthians 1:13 when a reader does not understand Paul?
A. Paul wrote deliberately deep so that his apostleship would be proven
B. Paul wrote nothing that cannot be understood, so the reader has basics to learn
C. A rhema word from the Spirit is needed before the text is understood
D. Only trained scholars can ever reach Paul's meaning in his letters
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: Reading 2 Corinthians 1:13, the speaker says Paul wrote nothing you cannot read and understand, so if you don't understand, there are basic things you need to learn.

Q105. In what order does the speaker present the first three common barriers to Bible interpretation?

B. Language, figures of speech, culture
C. Culture, language, figures of speech
D. Figures of speech, language, culture
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker says number one is language, the second thing is that the Bible is replete with figures of speech, and the third barrier is culture.

Q106. What does the speaker say can easily and cheaply correct language barriers?

C. Waiting for a rhema word on difficult passages

ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker says language barriers can easily and cheaply be corrected by using simpler translations, comparing good ones such as ESV, NIV and NLT.

Q128. What does the speaker say 'diverse manners' implies about how God spoke in the Old Testament?

Q131. What does the speaker say 'types and shadows' are?

Q149. How does the speaker define typology?

Q150. What does the speaker say the writer of Hebrews clarifies about the blood of bulls and goats?
A. It cannot take away sins; Jesus did it once and for all
B. It covered Israel's ceremonial sins but never moral guilt
C. It was accepted by God only for sins done unintentionally
D. It could remove sins only temporarily until the next feast
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker says Moses preached forgiveness by slaughtering lambs, but Hebrews clarifies the blood of bulls and goats cannot take away sins; Jesus did it once and for all.
REF: HERMENEUTICS (PART 2) II — [10:54]
BIBLE: Added from online research: Hebrews 9:11–14 (https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%209:11-14&version=ESV); Hebrews 10:4–14 (https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2010:4-14&version=ESV)

Q151. How does the speaker distinguish Old Testament circumcision from medical circumcision?
A. It was performed to mark a boy's passage to physical maturity
B. It involved cutting away more than the medical procedure does
C. It was a medical procedure meant to prevent disease in infants
D. It was symbolic, just a slit with some blood, rather than medical
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker says medical circumcision is mostly for aesthetics, but the Old Testament one was more symbolic, just a slit with some blood.
REF: HERMENEUTICS (PART 2) II — [11:44]
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Colossians 2:11

Q152. According to the speaker, what does 'the circumcision made without hands' in Colossians 2:11 refer to?
A. The Old Testament rite performed by the priests of Israel
B. The rite of baptism as practiced in the New Testament
C. The cutting of the heart through personal repentance alone
D. The putting off of the body of sins by Christ's circumcision
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker says the real circumcision is made without hands, in the putting off of the body of sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ.
REF: HERMENEUTICS (PART 2) II — [11:44; 12:41]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Colossians 2:11 | Also cited in lesson segment: Ezekiel 36:26

Q153. What does the speaker say Ezekiel 36:26 describes?
A. The true circumcision: stony heart removed, heart of flesh given
B. The judgment awaiting Israel's disobedient priests and kings
C. The ordinance of circumcision first given to Abraham's household
D. The rebuilding of the temple after the long exile in Babylon
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker cites Ezekiel 36:26 for the real circumcision, where God takes away the stony heart and puts His Spirit in us, so sinful propensity is removed by His Spirit.
REF: HERMENEUTICS (PART 2) II — [12:41; 13:38]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Ezekiel 36:26; Colossians 2:11

Q154. Whom does the speaker say Paul warns against in Philippians 3:2 with 'beware of the concision'?
A. Teachers who deny the bodily resurrection of Christ
B. Leaders who demand payment in exchange for their teaching
C. Believers who return to observing Jewish festivals and sabbaths
D. Those who still want to cut the flesh after the real circumcision
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker reads 'beware of the concision' as beware of people who still want to slit your flesh when the real circumcision is available by faith in Christ.
REF: HERMENEUTICS (PART 2) II — [14:44]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Philippians 3:2

Q155. What does the speaker say proves that Old Testament sacrifices were a type and shadow (Hebrews 10:1)?
A. They were eventually replaced by regular temple services and feasts
B. They had to be repeated year by year; one perfecting sacrifice would suffice
C. They were accepted by God only for sins committed in ignorance
D. They were offered only by the priests of Israel at the temple
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker says the proof that they were a type and shadow was that they had to do it every year; if it was efficacious enough, one would be enough.
REF: HERMENEUTICS (PART 2) II — [16:44]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Hebrews 10:1

Q156. What criterion does the speaker give for identifying a type in the Old Testament?
A. It must resemble the life and ministry of Christ closely
B. It must have been confirmed by the early church fathers
C. It must be clearly identified as a type in the New Testament
D. It must have been explained as a type by the later prophets
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: In the assignment, the speaker says you are not making it up; it must have been clearly identified as a type in the New Testament.
REF: HERMENEUTICS (PART 2) II — [18:31]
